column2: On the heart the number of elements; on the feet six stars; one should place the name-star clearly in the middle of the wheel:
eyes, head, right ear, right hand and feet; heart, neck, left hand; again the secret place and feet.
In whichever star the Sun stands, Saturn, Mars and Rahu, when one stays in that place one should know slaughter itself; no doubt.
I shall tell the Victory wheel: one should write from A to Ha; having drawn thirteen lines, one should draw six lines across.
Directions, planets, sages, suns, priests, Rudras, lunar days in order; musical modes, memories, Vedas, stars, Jinas; A, Ka, Da, Ma below.
Divided by seven the Sun and the others at the end of the name — the planets are strong: those called Sun, Saturn and Mars; the benefics for victory and alliance.
Having drawn twelve lines and six, those going and those northern; Manu and stars, in the eyes the sun's orb;
lunar days, flavors, Vedas, fire, or seventeen; Vasus and openings are declared; one should place A, Ka, Ta, Pa below.
Having placed each letter one by one, one should place the rest thus in order. Then one should divide the sum made of the name's letters by eight;
from the crow the circle is far forward; from the circle the ass is better; from the ass the bull is best; from the bull the elephant is better;
from the elephant again the lion; from the lion the... ass; the strong smoky one — thus the strength and weakness.
The gods in the A group; the Daityas rest in the Ka group; Nagas are the Cha group; Gandharvas born of the Ta group;
in the Ta group sages are declared; in the Pa group Rakshasas are remembered; Pishachas in the Ya group; men in the Sha group.
Daityas are stronger than gods, serpents than Daityas; Gandharvas than serpents; sages are better than Gandharvas;
Rakshasas are heroes over sages; Pishachas over Rakshasas; men over Pishachas; the strong should avoid the weak.
Again I tell the division of friends; hear the star wheel in order. Having made the first letter of the name the star clearly,
the stars standing in the star are nine and three in order: Janma, Sampat, Vipat, Kshema — these are the stars from the name-star;
Pratyara, Dhanada the sixth, Naidhana, Maitra, others; Paramaitra the last star; the Janma star is inauspicious;
Sampat star greatly best; Vipat star fruitless; Kshema star in all works; Pratyara destroys wealth;
Dhanada gives kingdom gain and the like; Naidhana destroys work; Maitra for friends; Paramitra brings welfare.
The star wheel. The vowel-measure is called the "matra"; one should put it in the middle of the name, beloved; divided by twenty, whatever remains is the fruit.
In the middle of the two measures one should mark wealth and debt; less measure is known as debt; more measure again as wealth.
By wealth there is friendship among men; by debt, indifference. This is the service wheel, showing gain and loss and the like.
Between Aries and Gemini fondness; friendship between Gemini and Leo; Libra and Leo great friendship; so Sagittarius and Aquarius;
one should not serve a friend; Pisces and Taurus are held friends; friendship of Taurus and Cancer; Cancer and Aquarius likewise;
Virgo and Scorpio thus; likewise Capricorn and Scorpio; Pisces and Capricorn friendly, placed third and eleventh;
Libra and Aries great friendship; Taurus and Scorpio hostile; fondness of Gemini and Sagittarius; Cancer and Capricorn likewise;
fondness of Capricorn and Aquarius; Virgo and Pisces likewise.
One should repeat a hundred and eight times in front of the enemy army; at the sound of the damaru by that repetition they drop their weapons and flee.
Hear the defeat of the enemy army; I shall tell it again by application: having taken charcoal from a cremation ground, and dung of owl and crow,
having drawn an image on cloth, with the letters of the target; having written the name nine times, in order, of the enemy:
on head, mouth, forehead, heart, secret place and feet, on the back and between the arms one should write the name nine times.
At the time of battle one should crush it, uttering the knowledge. I shall tell the Tarkshya wheel for victory, of three-faced syllables:
Kshipa Om svaha — the Tarkshya Self destroys enemies, disease, poison and the like; for one afflicted by evil beings and seizers, for the sick and the weak,
whatever work he does, such is accomplished by the bird. Immovable or movable poison, spiders, and artificial poison —
all that goes to destruction by the seeker's glance. Again one should meditate on great Tarkshya, two-winged, of human form,
two-armed, hooked-beaked, bearing elephant and tortoise, the lord, standing on the feet of countless serpents, coming from mid-sky,
swallowing, eating and piercing enemies in battle; some are to be seen struck by the beak, some crushed by the feet,
some crushed by wing-beats, some lost in the ten directions. He who is endowed with meditation on Tarkshya becomes unconquered in the three worlds.

I shall tell the Pichchhika, the rite born of mantra practice: "Om Hrum, bird, cast; Om Hum Sah, of great strength and valor, devour all the army, devour; Om crush, crush; Om pulverize, pulverize; Om scatter, scatter; Om Hum Khah; Om Bhairava commands, svaha." At a lunar eclipse having repeated and consecrated the Pichchhika,
one should wave it, causing the army in front of elephants and lions to turn; by meditation one should crush those running, mounted on a lion, deer and sheep.
I shall tell defeat by sound: one should awaken it from afar by mantra. One should give porridge to the Mothers, especially to Kalaratri,
mixed with cremation-ash, malati and chamari, only cotton root; by that one should awaken from afar.

Om Ahe he Mahendri, Ahe Mahendri, break; Om kill, devour, devour, kili kili kili; Om Hum phat — by the repeated defeat-knowledge, destruction of foes from the distant sound; aparajita and datura — with those a tilaka.

Om kili kili vikili ichchhakili, bhutahani, shankhini, both, staff-handed, Raudri Maheshvari, Ulkamukhi, Jvalamukhi, Shankukarne, Shushkajanghe, Alambushe, take Om; destroy all evils; Om whatever one looks upon, goddess, bewilder those; Om, Raudri, abiding in Rudra's heart with a gentle mood, do self-protection at the end, svaha. Having drawn the Mothers outside surrounded with all forms, one should write the knowledge on a nagapatra, fulfilling all desires,
held earlier by hands and the rest by Brahma, Rudra, Indra and Vishnu; in the time of the great battle the gods were protected by the knowledge,
by Raksha, Narasimhi, Bhairavi of the form of Shakti, by the enchantress of the three worlds, Gauri, in the war of gods and demons.
The name enclosed with seed-syllables in the pericarp and in the petals; by the order of worship the limbs — the protection-yantra is remembered, auspicious one.
I shall tell Mrityunjaya in the middle of the name-rite: enclosed by digits, awakened afterward by the letter Sa,
the letter Ja with bindu, joined with Om; in the middle of the belly of Dha, awakened by the letter Va,
standing in the middle of the moon-enclosure, destroyer of all evil. Or in the pericarp one should write the name and the cause;
in the east petal likewise Om, in its right and north; in the southeast and so on Hum; in the sixteen petals the vowels;
in the thirty-four petals Ka and the rest; outside, the Mrityunjaya mantra; one should write on birch-bark with rochana and saffron,
with camphor and sandal, enclose with white thread; having covered with wax one should worship above a pot.
By wearing the yantra passions are quieted, enemies die. I shall tell the knowledge Bhelakhi, remover of separation and death:

Om Vatale Vitale Vidalamukhi Indraputri... [a string of syllables] "Om Bhelakhi, Om svaha" — repeated seven times with Navadurga, a mouth-paralysis from what stands in the mouth; "Om Chandi, Om Hum phat svaha" — having taken it seven times recited, unconquered in a sword fight.
Always by oblation, repetition and recital and the rest there is victory in battle. One should meditate her twenty-eight-armed, with sword and shield in the hands,
two others with mace and staff; others bearing arrow and bow; both with fist and club; others with conch and sword;
others bearing banner and thunderbolt; others with discus and axe; with drum and mirror; others bearing spear and lance;
with plow and pestle; with noose and spear; with drum and tabor; with fearless gesture and fist;
threatening the buffalo, the slayer; by oblation the conqueror of enemies. The oblation is with sesame mixed with three sweets; it should not be given to just anyone.
This is the first channel, and another: Yamya, Mrigashira, Pushya, Bhagya, Chitra, Maitra, Apya and Vasava;
Ahirbudhnya the third; Krittika, Rohini, Ahi; Chitra, Svati, Vishakha, Shravana and Revati — the star.
By the planets joined with the three channels one should know the auspicious and inauspicious. This wheel, Phanishvara, is adorned with three channels;
standing on Sun, Mars, Saturn and Rahu it is inauspicious; otherwise auspicious. Brothers, wives and the rest with regions and villages are each auspicious.
Licking, terrible, fierce with fangs, fearful; by the fall of his glance horses and the like are eaten;
the third is the Goddess's face, white-hued, destroying elephants and the like; with scent, flowers and the like, honey and ghee, one should worship facing west.
By remembering the mantra, diseases of the eye, head and so on perish; Yakshas and Rakshasas come under control and enemies go to destruction.
Fuel sticks of neem mixed with goat's blood, one should kill, joined with anger, by oblation alone; no doubt.
If one offers for a week facing the enemy army, the army is seized by diseases and the enemy is defeated.
Whoever's name one offers eight thousand sticks for dies soon, even if protected by Brahma.
A thousand datura sticks mixed with red poison — in three days the enemy with his army goes to destruction.
By oblation with mustard and salt, defeat of the enemy in three days; by oblation mixed with donkey's blood one should expel the enemy;
by oblation joined with crow's blood, destruction of the enemy. It does all for the killing, whatever is desired in mind.
Then at the time of battle the seeker, mounted on an elephant, with two maidens, his body armored with mantras,
should consecrate by the knowledge the distant conch and other instruments; having taken the Mahamaya cloth, it should be raised in the battlefield;
facing the enemy army one should show that great cloth. One should feed maidens there and afterward whirl the lump of food.
The seeker should think of the army as immovable like stone; he should imagine it dispirited, broken and bewildered.
This paralysis has been told by me; it should not be given to just anyone. Mahamaya, victorious in the three worlds, Durga, Bhairavi likewise,
Kubjika, Bhairava, Rudra, with the Narasimha cloth and the like.
Again at the end one should write the mantra, the target and the mantra-word again. The restraining tradition should be applied in paralysis and the like.
Below and above, right and left, in the middle one should place the target. That is to be known as the Samputa; one should apply it in subjugation and attraction.
When the mantra-letters are the target, strung letter by letter — that is the first tradition, attracting and subjugating.
Having written two mantra-letters and one target-letter again — that is to be known as Vidarbha; one should apply it in subjugation and attraction.
The work from attraction one should do in spring. In fever-heat and subjugation, "svaha" is good in attraction;
the word "namah" one should use in peace and growth; "vashat" in nourishing rites, attraction and subjugation;
phat in hatred, expulsion and death; in divided rites auspicious; in gain and the like and mantra-initiation "vashat" gives accomplishment.
You are Yama, you are King of Death, you are of the form of Time, king of Dharma; this enemy given by me, fell him quickly.
I fell him with effort; turn back, seeker — with a joyful mind the teacher, destroyer of foes, should say.
Having worshipped Yama on a white lotus, this is accomplished by oblation. Having meditated on oneself as Bhairava, then in the middle Kuleshvari,
